title: Iterator Adapters
concept: Iterator adapters transform iterators into new iterators — map, filter, take, skip, chain, zip, and more. They compose like building blocks.
why: Instead of writing loops for every transformation, adapter chaining expresses complex data pipelines declaratively — more readable and less error-prone.
theory:
## Transforming Iterators

### map — Apply a Function
```xiom
let nums = Vec[Int](); nums.push(1); nums.push(2); nums.push(3);
let squares = nums.iter().map(|n| n * n);
// Produces: 1, 4, 9
```

### filter — Keep Matching Elements
```xiom
let evens = nums.iter().filter(|n| n % 2 == 0);
// Produces: 2
```

### Chaining Adapters
```xiom
let result = nums.iter()
  .filter(|n| n % 2 == 0)   // Keep evens: 2
  .map(|n| n * n)             // Square them: 4
  .collect();                  // Collect to Vec: [4]
```

### Common Adapters

| Adapter | What It Does |
|---------|-------------|
| .map(f) | Transform each element |
| .filter(p) | Keep elements where p is true |
| .take(n) | Take first n elements |
| .skip(n) | Skip first n elements |
| .chain(other) | Concatenate two iterators |
| .enumerate() | Add index: (0, item), (1, item), ... |
| .zip(other) | Pair elements: (a1,b1), (a2,b2), ... |
| .rev() | Reverse the iterator |

### Complex Pipeline
```xiom
fn top_scores(scores: &Vec[Int], n: Int) -> Vec[Int] {
  return scores.iter()
    .filter(|s| s >= 60)     // Passing only
    .sorted()                  // Sort ascending
    .rev()                     // Reverse to descending
    .take(n)                   // Top n scores
    .collect();
}
```
syntax_ref:
iter.map(|x| transform(x))    // Transform
  .filter(|x| condition(x)) // Filter
  .take(n)                  // Limit
  .skip(n)                  // Offset
  .collect()                // Materialize
tips: Adapters are LAZY — they don't do anything until you consume the iterator (.collect(), .fold(), for loop)
Chain adapters in logical order: filter → map → take/skip → collect
Each adapter creates a NEW iterator — zero allocation for the pipeline itself
Use .inspect(|x| io.println(x)) to debug iterator pipelines
common_mistakes: Expecting adapters to modify the original collection — they create new iterators
Chaining adapters in the wrong order — filter before map is more efficient
Forgetting to consume the iterator — adapters alone don't execute anything
